final:
Only 1 of the 10 review comments needs a fix: `BackupCode.tsx` names its component `TwoFactor`. Another 6 are partly right or worth considering, and 3 don't hold up. I didn't change any code or post replies. The verdicts are in `verdicts.json`, 10 entries.

| Verdict | Count | IDs |
|---|---|---|
| VALID (needs a fix) | 1 | 4 |
| VALID (optional) | 1 | 7 |
| PARTIALLY_VALID (optional) | 4 | 3, 5, 6, 9 |
| STYLE_PREFERENCE | 2 | 2, 8 |
| INVALID | 2 | 0, 1 |

- **#4 (valid, needs a fix):** `apps/web/components/auth/BackupCode.tsx:7` is `export default function TwoFactor`, left over from copying the existing component. The imports still work because it's a default export, but the component shows up as "TwoFactor" in React DevTools and error traces. The fix is a one-word rename.
- **#7 (valid, optional):** backup-code login and disabling 2FA with a backup code have no tests. The author already noted this in a TODO at `login.2fa.e2e.ts:12`. These are login paths that skip the authenticator app, so tests are worth adding.
- **#5 (partly valid):** `resetState` leaves the backup codes, the 2FA secret and the QR code in memory. The modal never unmounts, so they stay there after it closes. Two of the reviewer's points are wrong, though:
  - `isSubmitting` is already reset in a `finally` block.
  - The old download URL is already revoked before a new one is created (`EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:98`).
- **#9 (partly valid):** the download URL isn't released when the component unmounts. That's true, but the most it can hold is one blob of about 120 bytes.
- **#3 (partly valid):** once all backup codes are used, the user gets "Backup code is incorrect" instead of a clearer message. But the suggested "regenerate codes" fix doesn't exist in this PR; the only way to get new codes is to set up 2FA again.
- **#6 (partly valid):** the input already requires a value and limits its length (10–11 characters). A small gap remains: 9 code characters plus a dash is accepted, and characters outside `0-9a-f` aren't rejected before sending. The server rejects these anyway, so this is only a usability improvement.
- **#0 (invalid):** the reviewer says the rest of the file returns errors instead of throwing. That's wrong: `disable.ts` already throws in the same situations at lines 77, 82 and 90, and the new code follows that pattern.
- **#1 (invalid):** setting a used code to `null` can't fill the array up over time. It always has exactly 10 slots, it's replaced on every setup and cleared on disable, and a `null` slot can never match a typed code.
- **#2 and #8 (style):** the nested ternary at `login.tsx:221` is harder to read but behaves correctly. `formatBackupCode` being declared after `handleSetup` can't fail at runtime, because `handleSetup` only runs on form submit, after the component has rendered.
